answer: The strongest lever is simple: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because comet only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. In practice velvet is enforced by the ledger itself: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any haven approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
